subject: Fieldstone committed plan — throughput gap & GPU safety strip
messages:

Subject: Initial throughput inputs — Fieldstone Dedicated commitment

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, to convert the pilot into a Dedicated commitment we need a concrete throughput/latency alignment and a recommended GPU slab that fits your SLOs while leaving operational headroom.

Can you attach a sample of hourly token volumes for your top 3 endpoints, and confirm: average output length (tokens) per request, expected peak concurrent requests, and any quiet hours profile? The attached "fieldstone_usage_sample.csv" is a placeholder you can fill.

Next steps on our side: Priyom will run a targeted throughput model (tokens/sec per GPU) for your preferred model family and propose a safety strip (buffer) and a cost/commitment mapping. We usually size two lanes: 1) baseline committed slab to meet p95 SLO during business hours, and 2) burst lane with on-demand capacity for spikes.

I attached a working spreadsheet (rwi-throughput-estimate-v1.xlsx) with the fields we need. If procurement wants to loop in someone for the contract cadence, add them to CC.

Best,
Rishi
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

Rishi —

Thanks. I filled the usage sample and attached. Quick clarifications:
- Average model response length by endpoint: SearchAssist ~60 tokens, Summarize ~200 tokens, ChatAssist ~120 tokens.
- Peak concurrent requests historically during morning rollouts: ~1,100 req/s across endpoints (combined).
- Quiet hours: overnight traffic drops to ~8% of peak.
- Target SLO: p95 latency < 300ms for prompt -> first token, and p99 tail < 1s for incremental streaming.

We prefer the rw-7b-family you demoed and are open to a 7b quantized profile if it meets the latency targets. Procurement is copied for timing on the contract.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput inputs — Fieldstone Dedicated commitment

Alice / Rishi,

Thanks for the sample, that helps. I ran a micro-benchmark and a capacity model targeting the rw-7b-quant-4 profile using our internal benchmark harness (128-token avg output, batching window 20ms, concurrency up to 32). Key results below:

- Observed sustained throughput per A100-80GB (q4x) under realistic batching: ~2,600 tokens/sec (median).
- Under synthetic peak batching (aggressive coalescing) we see up to ~3,900 tokens/sec per GPU, but that relies on steady stream and adds latency for single-request tails.
- For your p95 <300ms (first-token) target, we recommend using the conservative sustained number: 2,200 tokens/sec per GPU (this factors in KV cache variability, input length variance, and background GC).

Sizing math (peak planning):
- Peak observed combined concurrency ~1,100 req/s with weighted avg output length 120 tokens => ~132,000 tokens/sec peak.
- Using 2,200 tokens/sec per GPU => required GPUs (no headroom) = 132,000 / 2,200 ≈ 60 GPUs.
- We recommend a safety strip of 40% for peak headroom and transient spikes (network jitter, cache warmup, canary traffic) => target committed slab = 84 GPUs (rounded).
- Additionally suggest a small burst pool of 12 on-demand GPUs for rare sustained spikes beyond the safety strip.

Operational notes:
- If you can reduce average response length via truncated summaries or higher-temperature sampling cutoffs during spikes, effective tokens/sec requirement drops substantially.
- Quantization trade: q4 gives best cost/throughput for 7b; moving to 3b reduces GPU count but may impact output fidelity for some tasks. We can run a targeted eval on your prompt set.

I'll attach the detailed workbook (rwi-throughput-estimate-v1.xlsx) with the scenario tabs. Ben, can you draft a pricing sketch for 84-GPU monthly commitment + burst-on-demand pricing?

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: rwi-throughput-estimate-v1.xlsx

Subject: Re: Initial throughput inputs — Fieldstone Dedicated commitment

Looping in pricing & commercial. Quick commercial framing for FS-2028-042:

- Proposed committed slab: 84 A100-equivalent GPUs (monthly term, 12-month commitment) — list price sketch attached.
- Burst policy: 12 GPUs on-demand billed at metered spike rate, auto-fallback to region pool if on-demand exhausted.
- SLA: p95 latency objective baked into the runbook with automatic fallback to a 7b-alt model hosted in another region if local slab is saturated (we'll keep a warm standby, costed as a small monthly retention).

Discounting note: To land reasonable unit economics for the customer we should consider a 16-20% commit discount for a 12-month term. Rishi — do you want to propose a pilot-to-commit trade (e.g., 2-week pilot with 50% credit applied to first month of the committed slab)?

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Thank you — the numbers are reasonable and the safety strip feels right given our launch cadence. A few asks from procurement/ops:

1) Can Redwood provide a short evaluation run with our top 20 prompts on rw-7b-quant-4 to validate quality vs rw-3b and confirm the 2,200 tok/s baseline per GPU?
2) Please include a clause for scheduled quiet-hour autoscaling (we want guaranteed scaling down to no less than 20% of committed slab for cost predictability).
3) Provide a simple SLA rollback path if p95 breaches occur for >3 consecutive days during launch week.

If you can provide the evaluation artifact and a redlined service-level-proposal, procurement will prepare an initial PO. Intent to sign subject to evaluation and a pilot credit applied to month 1.

Best,
Alice

I'll wait for Priyom and Ben drafts and then connect procurement to finalize the PO path. If any of the internal numbers look off, quote them back — I want the explicit math in the contract appendix.
